title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact‑Backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to test whether a composite canary–rollback operational score discriminates emulator‑measured outages better than any single submetric. Using a synthetic NetOps task bank and a deterministic validator we ran 200 held‑out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded) and preserved exhaustive artifacts (raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace, provider-call traces, execution manifest, and full SHA‑256 hashes). All 200 test pairs validated successfully in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). Paired‑bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC‑ROC primary estimand is undefined on this held‑out set because labels are constant. Two preregistered artifacts required to recompute the AUC comparison (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are absent from the preserved bundle; we (i) map each principal claim to exact persisted artifact path(s) and SHA‑256, (ii) provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe limited to preserved artifacts, and (iii) give an explicit artifact‑hygiene checklist required to enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations in future runs.

sections.introduction: Modern NetOps proposals increasingly employ agentic LLMs to translate operator intent into device configurations. Operational adoption requires evidence that LLM‑proposed changes are safe: deterministic validators, canary simulation, rollback trials, and abstention policies are common safeguards. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to ask a specific, confirmable question: can a composite canary–rollback score (a linear combination of verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) predict emulator‑measured outages better than the best single submetric? The preregistration (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee) fixed the model family (gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the synthetic task bank split (train=300,val=100,test=200), metrics, and the analysis pipeline (L2 with CV; primary comparison: AUC‑ROC composite vs best submetric). We executed the frozen plan and preserved exhaustive, hashed artifacts (execution manifest, per‑episode scoring JSONs containing validator_trace, provider-call traces, raw responses, and analysis CSVs). The actual held‑out outcome is a valid, artifact‑grounded null: every held‑out candidate passed validation in both conditions, rendering the AUC comparison undefined. Rather than claiming a positive discriminative result, this paper documents the executed run, proves the paired null from persisted artifacts, diagnoses missing persisted artifacts that block full recomputation of the preregistered pipeline, provides a deterministic reconstruction recipe constrained to preserved artifacts, and supplies an actionable artifact‑hygiene checklist for future discriminative evaluations.
sections.related_work: The study is positioned at the intersection of (1) generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines for operationally constrained generation, (2) verifier orchestration and cost‑aware verification policies, and (3) reproducibility/provenance practices for computational experiments. Prior work demonstrates architectures that interpose verifiers and canary/rollback trials to convert stochastic LLM proposals into enforceable changes; evaluation literature argues for workflow‑centred metrics beyond static QA. Our contribution is not a new verifier or agent architecture: it is an artifact‑grounded empirical reproducibility report of a preregistered discriminative evaluation attempt for composite operational scoring, documenting what the preserved evidence supports and precisely which persisted artifacts are missing for recomputability of the originally prespecified AUC analysis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 (JSON SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task bank: synthetic deterministic generator with fixed deterministic split (train=300,val=100,test=200) and deterministic seeds recorded per task. Experimental design. Paired binary design: for each test task we generated a shared_initial candidate and evaluated two guardedness conditions (baseline vs guarded) where guarded condition applied runtime safeguards (the run used a shared_initial generation policy; shared response reused across conditions). Planned episodes: 400 (200 pairs). Maximum model calls: 400; model_calls_used reported in the manifest = 200 (shared_initial only; see execution/execution_manifest.json). Metrics and analysis (frozen): extract per‑episode submetrics (verifier_coverage = observed_touched_field_count/required_command_count; canary_sim_pass boolean; rollback_success_prob numeric; LLM_confidence numeric; abstention_utility numeric), train penalized logistic regression (L2) mapping submetrics to binary outage label on train+val via 5‑fold CV, freeze weights, evaluate AUC‑ROC on test, compare composite vs best single submetric using DeLong; compute paired bootstrap CI (seed=1729,R=10000) for paired differences. Artifact capture. The run preserved: raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scoring JSONs including full validator_trace (execution/scoring/*.json), provider‑call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), execution manifest and per‑artifact SHA‑256 hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv). Scorer semantics. Each execution/scoring/<episode>.json contains validator_trace.validation_after.{normalized_configuration,final_state,parsed_command_count,required_command_count,observed_touched_field_count,valid} and score with reason_code VALID_CONFIGURATION when valid. These fields are the canonical extractor for verifier_coverage.
sections.results: Artifact‑grounded empirical facts. Execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200; per‑artifact hashes are preserved in the manifest. Held‑out test empirical counts (derived from execution/scoring/*.json and consolidated into analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) are: baseline_success_count = 200/200; guarded_success_count = 200/200; paired contingency: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. These counts are explicit in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). Inferential calculations performed from preserved artifacts: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d). Exact McNemar two‑sided test (pre‑registered) computed from the same contingency table yields p = 1.0 (analysis artifacts). Status of preregistered primary estimand. The preregistered primary estimand (AUC‑ROC difference composite vs best submetric on held‑out test) is uncomputable from the preserved bundle because the test labels are constant (no outage positives): ROC/AUPRC require both classes present; AUC is undefined when one class is absent. Missing persisted artifacts that block composite pipeline recomputation. The preregistration required two runtime‑produced artifacts that are not present in the preserved manifest: (1) consolidated_submetrics.csv (per‑episode rows with verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) and (2) composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized L2 coefficients and normalization metadata). These filenames are the canonical artifacts declared in the preregistration; their absence prevents recomputing the preregistered composite model and therefore the AUC comparison without re‑execution. Submetric availability (artifact‑grounded). From the preserved scoring and provider traces we determine: - verifier_coverage: PRESENT — computable from execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and required_command_count (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478). - canary_sim_pass: ABSENT — no canary_sim_* boolean or deterministic canary log lines found in execution/provider_calls/*.json or execution/scoring/*.json. - rollback_success_prob: ABSENT — no rollback trial outputs or probabilities present in preserved provider_call traces. - LLM_confidence: ABSENT — provider_call traces do not contain a persistent numeric confidence field in preserved bundle. - abstention_utility: ABSENT — no preserved abstention metric. Deterministic reconstruction recipe (artifact‑limited). Using preserved artifacts one can: (1) recompute per‑episode binary labels as validator_trace.validation_after.valid from execution/scoring/*.json; (2) compute verifier_coverage per episode from observed_touched_field_count / required_command_count (execution/scoring/*.json); (3) assemble the paired contingency table and reproduce McNemar/bootstrap inference from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (both preserved); (4) to complete the preregistered composite pipeline one of the following is required and is NOT present: (a) the consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl persisted at runtime, or (b) the deterministic canary and rollback logs (canary_simulator_log.json and rollback_trial_log.json) plus preserved instructions and seeds to deterministically reconstruct canary/rollback outputs, and then retrain the L2 model with the original RNG seed. Representative episode example. execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2b...) contains validator_trace.validation_after with normalized_configuration, final_state, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count and valid=true; the shared_initial candidate is at execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...). These artifacts concretely support the reported paired counts and the paired contingency table.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The preserved evidence shows a legitimate ceiling outcome: under the frozen design and synthetic task bank, the validator predicates accepted every generated candidate in both conditions on the held‑out partition. This outcome is scientifically informative: it shows that, for this deterministic generator + validator configuration, the held‑out tasks produced no emulator outages and therefore discriminative tests requiring both positive and negative labels are inapplicable. Operational implication. Discriminative evaluation of composite safety scores requires held‑out partitions that include adverse outcomes; practical strategies include injecting adversarial tasks, fault‑injection into the emulator, or reserving a stratified test set with higher‑difficulty/perturbation cases. Reproducibility diagnosis and remediation. The evidence bundle is sufficient to (i) verify the paired null counts and reproduce paired bootstrap/McNemar calculations (artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1b..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = c56b7...), and (ii) recompute verifier_coverage per episode (execution/scoring/*.json). However, the bundle lacks the consolidated per‑episode submetric CSV and the serialized trained composite model needed to recompute the preregistered AUC comparison. Deterministic reconstruction without re‑execution requires either (a) those two missing persisted artifacts, or (b) preserved deterministic canary and rollback logs and a preserved retrain script with RNG seed; neither is present. Artifact‑hygiene checklist (actionable, exact filenames & canonical fields). To make future runs fully reproducible for discriminative AUC comparisons we recommend persisting at runtime these exact files and canonical fields: 1) consolidated_submetrics.csv — columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility (CSV). 2) composite_model_weights.pkl — serialized L2 coefficients, intercept, feature normalization metadata, and training RNG seed. 3) canary_simulator_log.json — deterministic per‑episode canary simulator outputs (fields: episode_id,canary_seed,canary_result_boolean,canary_trace_sha256). 4) rollback_trial_log.json — deterministic per‑episode rollback trial outputs (fields: episode_id,rollback_seed,rollback_success_prob,rollback_trace_sha256). 5) retrain_script.py plus requirements.txt with pinned package versions and the RNG seed used for training. These preserved files would allow recomputation of the preregistered pipeline without re‑calling model endpoints. Threats to validity. Internal: using shared_initial generation reduces variance and isolates guard machinery but can mask prompt sensitivity. Construct: emulator labels approximate outage risk but may not capture device nondeterminism. External: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks limit generality. Missingness: absent consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl prevent recomputation of the primary AUC estimand from the preserved bundle.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered deterministic paired study and archived exhaustive hashed artifacts. The held‑out test produced a ceiling outcome: every candidate validated in both baseline and guarded conditions (n11=200), making the AUC‑ROC primary estimand undefined on the preserved bundle. Two preregistered runtime artifacts necessary to reconstruct the preregistered composite pipeline (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are missing from the manifest and thus the composite‑vs‑single AUC comparison cannot be recomputed solely from the supplied artifacts. We (i) map each principal claim to exact artifact paths and SHA‑256, (ii) provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe constrained to preserved artifacts, and (iii) provide a concrete artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames and canonical fields) to enable non‑degenerate, fully reproducible discriminative evaluations in future agentic NetOps studies.

disclosure_statement: Human and autonomy boundary. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 and the preregistration JSON SHA‑256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee. Persisted artifacts and representative SHA‑256 references (exact, from the evidence bundle). execution/execution_manifest.json (full-per-artifact manifest and hashes); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951); analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d); execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478); execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). Missing preregistered persisted artifacts (artifact-grounded). The preregistration required consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl; neither file is present in the preserved manifest and therefore the preregistered AUC‑ROC comparison cannot be recomputed from the bundle alone. Safety and operational scope. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). No human manual manuscript editing occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real‑world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented execution artifact-collection omission).
